rationale: Anchor: the statistical-model consensus (median across methods) from compare_forecast_models, which sits at 16.9k/21.2k/25.6k/31.6k for h0-h3. I trimmed the h0-h2 medians slightly toward the backtest-best methods (seasonal MAE 1349, gbt 2469, loglinear 1630) to 16.5k/20.0k/23.5k, and set h3 at 27.0k, below the seasonal analogue's 41k because last year's peak (42.5k in early Jan) came ~6 weeks after this point with growth still accelerating, whereas this season's growth is decelerating (+33% -> +16% -> +14% wk/wk) and the season started earlier (mid-October high activity, 7 states at high ILI by Nov 7), implying the peak arrives sooner and the h3 week is closer to it. The hub ensemble had no submission for this week, so I had no ensemble prior to lean on; the flat baseline (11.5k) is clearly wrong given the rising trajectory. Evidence for the upward tilt vs persistence: ILI at 3.23% and still rising, 11.3% of lab tests positive, CDC reporting an early season with 36k hospitalizations already, and last year from this exact point admissions went 11.5k -> 21k -> 37.5k -> 42.5k. I keep the medians below the seasonal analogue because the decelerating growth rate and earlier start argue for a flatter, earlier peak. Intervals are lognormal, right-skewed, and widened with horizon (sigma 0.16 -> 0.24) to cover the method disagreement (1.2-1.5x spread in medians), the upward revision risk in the provisional last week, and the possibility of a faster surge as Thanksgiving gatherings drive transmission. What would change my mind: if next week's actual comes in below ~15k (growth stalling), the whole trajectory is lower and the peak is modest; if it exceeds ~20k, the seasonal-analogue path is back in play and h2-h3 should be raised toward 30k-40k.
